[id="llama-stack-sdk-migration-reference_{context}"]
= Llama Stack SDK API changes in version 0.3.1

[role="_abstract"]
The Llama Stack SDK version 0.3.1 introduces breaking API changes that affect all vector store providers, including inline Milvus, remote Milvus, inline FAISS, and PostgreSQL with pgvector.
If you have existing Jupyter notebooks or scripts that use the Llama Stack SDK version 0.2.x, you must update your code to use the new API patterns.

Review the breaking changes, before-and-after code comparisons, and affected SDK methods to update your code.

== Summary of breaking changes

The following table lists the breaking API changes introduced in Llama Stack SDK version 0.3.1.

.Llama Stack SDK 0.3.1 breaking changes
[options="header"]
|===
|Change |Old API pattern (SDK 0.2.x) |New API pattern (SDK 0.3.1)

|Vector store creation
|`client.vector_dbs.register(vector_db_id=..., embedding_model=..., embedding_dimension=..., provider_id=...)`
|`client.vector_stores.create(name=..., extra_body={"embedding_model": ..., "embedding_dimension": ..., "provider_id": ...})`

|Document ingestion
|`RAGDocument` objects with `client.tool_runtime.rag_tool.insert()`
|`client.vector_stores.files.create(vector_store_id=..., file_id=..., chunking_strategy={...})`

|Content querying
|`client.tool_runtime.rag_tool.query()`
|`client.responses.create(tools=[{"type": "file_search", "vector_store_ids": [...]}])`

|Vector store identifier parameter
|`vector_db_id` and `vector_db_ids`
|`vector_store_id` and `vector_store_ids`

|Minimum SDK version
|`llama_stack_client >= 0.2.22`
|`llama_stack_client >= 0.3.1`

|`fire` dependency
|Required (`pip install fire`)
|Removed from dependencies
|===

== Vector store creation with `extra_body`

In SDK 0.3.1, you pass vector store creation parameters such as `embedding_model`, `embedding_dimension`, and `provider_id` inside an `extra_body` dictionary instead of as top-level keyword arguments.

.Old pattern (SDK 0.2.x)
[source,python]
----
vector_db = client.vector_dbs.register(
    vector_db_id="my_store",
    embedding_model=embedding_model_id,
    embedding_dimension=embedding_dimension,
    provider_id="milvus",
)
----

.New pattern (SDK 0.3.1)
[source,python]
----
vector_store = client.vector_stores.create(
    name="my_store",
    extra_body={
        "embedding_model": embedding_model_id,
        "embedding_dimension": embedding_dimension,
        "provider_id": "milvus",
    },
)
vector_store_id = vector_store.id
----

Verify that `vector_store.id` returns a non-empty string to confirm the vector store was created successfully.

This change applies to all vector store providers.
Replace the `provider_id` value with the provider that matches your deployment: `milvus` for inline Milvus, `milvus-remote` for remote Milvus, `faiss` for inline FAISS, or `pgvector` for PostgreSQL with pgvector.

== Document ingestion with the vector store files API

In SDK 0.3.1, document ingestion uses the `client.vector_stores.files.create()` method with file upload instead of the `RAGDocument` class and `rag_tool.insert()` method.

.Old pattern (SDK 0.2.x)
[source,python]
----
from llama_stack_client.types import RAGDocument

documents = [
    RAGDocument(
        document_id="doc-1",
        content="https://example.com/document.pdf",
        mime_type="application/pdf",
        metadata={},
    ),
]

client.tool_runtime.rag_tool.insert(
    tool_name="builtin::rag/knowledge_search",
    vector_db_id=vector_db_id,
    documents=documents,
    chunk_size_in_tokens=800,
)
----

.New pattern (SDK 0.3.1)
[source,python]
----
# Upload the file first
with open("document.pdf", "rb") as f:
    file_info = client.files.create(
        file=("document.pdf", f),
        purpose="assistants",
    )

# Add the file to a vector store with chunking
vector_store_file = client.vector_stores.files.create(
    vector_store_id=vector_store_id,
    file_id=file_info.id,
    chunking_strategy={
        "type": "static",
        "static": {
            "max_chunk_size_tokens": 800,
            "chunk_overlap_tokens": 400,
        },
    },
)
----

Verify that `vector_store_file.id` returns a non-empty string to confirm the file was ingested successfully.

The following list describes the key differences:

* SDK 0.3.1 removes the `RAGDocument` class. Remove it from your import statements.
* You must upload files to Llama Stack with `client.files.create()` before ingestion.
Documents must be available as local files.
URL-based document references, such as `content="https://example.com/document.pdf"`, are no longer directly supported.
If your existing code loads documents by URL, you must download the file to local storage before uploading it with `client.files.create()`.
* You specify chunking parameters in a `chunking_strategy` dictionary instead of as a `chunk_size_in_tokens` argument.
Tune the `chunk_overlap_tokens` value based on your use case.
The value of `400` in this example is a high overlap (50% of `max_chunk_size_tokens`) chosen for illustration.
A typical starting value is 100 to 200 tokens.
Higher overlap values increase index size but can improve retrieval quality for context-dependent content.
* The method returns metadata about the ingested file, which you can use for verification.

== Content querying with the responses API

In SDK 0.3.1, RAG queries use the `client.responses.create()` method with a `file_search` tool instead of the `rag_tool.query()` method.

.Old pattern (SDK 0.2.x)
[source,python]
----
response = client.tool_runtime.rag_tool.query(
    tool_name="builtin::rag/knowledge_search",
    vector_db_ids=[vector_db_id],
    content="What is retrieval-augmented generation?",
)
----

.New pattern (SDK 0.3.1)
[source,python]
----
response = client.responses.create(
    model=model_id,
    input="What is retrieval-augmented generation?",
    instructions="Use retrieved context when available.",
    tools=[
        {
            "type": "file_search",
            "vector_store_ids": [vector_store_id],
        }
    ],
)

print(response.output_text)
----

Verify that `response.output_text` contains a model-generated answer that incorporates the retrieved context from your ingested documents.

The following list describes the key differences:

* The `responses.create()` method with a `file_search` tool type replaces the `rag_tool.query()` method.
* The `response.output_text` attribute contains a model-generated answer that incorporates the retrieved context.
Unlike the old `rag_tool.query()` method, which returned raw retrieved chunks, the Responses API returns text generated by the LLM.
To access the raw retrieved chunks, inspect the `output` array in the full response object for file search results.
* You must specify the `model` parameter to indicate which LLM generates the response.
* Customize the `instructions` parameter for your specific use case to improve response quality.
For a more detailed example, see xref:querying-ingested-content-in-a-llama-model_{context}[Querying ingested content in a Llama model].

== Parameter rename: `vector_db_id` to `vector_store_id`

SDK 0.3.1 renames all occurrences of `vector_db_id` and `vector_db_ids` to `vector_store_id` and `vector_store_ids`.

.Affected parameters
[options="header"]
|===
|Old parameter name |New parameter name |Context

|`vector_db_id`
|`vector_store_id`
|Vector store creation, file ingestion, direct queries

|`vector_db_ids`
|`vector_store_ids`
|`file_search` tool configuration, agent tool arguments
|===

Update all references in your code, including any variables, function arguments, and configuration dictionaries that use the old naming convention.

== SDK installation

.Old installation (SDK 0.2.x)
[source,terminal]
----
%pip install llama_stack_client fire
----

.New installation (SDK 0.3.1)
[source,terminal]
----
%pip install llama_stack_client
----

The `%pip` command is a Jupyter notebook magic command.
If you are running the command outside a Jupyter notebook, use `pip install` instead.

The `fire` package is no longer required as a dependency.
Verify that your environment installs version 0.3.1 or later.
